issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Monte Carlo estimate of pi and how its error scales with the number of samples.

Estimate pi by sampling points uniformly in the unit square and counting those inside the quarter circle. For each N in 10^3, 10^4 and 10^5, run 50 independent estimates with `numpy.random.default_rng` seeded from 2026 plus the run index, and record the mean absolute error against `math.pi`.

Fit log(mean absolute error) against log(N) by least squares and give the exponent; compare it with the -1/2 expected for Monte Carlo.

Report: `report/report.md`, one short page with the table of N and mean absolute error and the fitted exponent.
